'''Creamed spinach''' makes a nutritious [[Cookbook:sauce|sauce]] that goes well with [[Cookbook:fish|fish]] and [[Cookbook:meat|meat]] dishes. In Swedish cuisine it has traditionally been used with boiled [[Cookbook:potatoes|potatoes]] and [[Cookbook:fish|fish]] or with chipolata, the Swedish "prince-sausage". Creamed spinach can be done in two different ways: either with whole spinach or with chopped spinach.

== Ingredients ==

=== Variation I – Whole spinach ===
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] fresh [[Cookbook:spinach|spinach]] (or whole frozen spinach leaves)
* 2 [[Cookbook:Deciliter|dl]] [[Cookbook:water|water]]
* ½ dl [[Cookbook:cream|cream]] or 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Black pepper]]

=== Variation II – Chopped spinach ===
* 400 g of [[Cookbook:chop|chopped]] spinach, fresh or frozen
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:flour|flour]]
* 1 dl [[Cookbook:milk|milk]]
* ½ tsp salt
* Black pepper

== Procedure ==

=== Variation I – Whole spinach ===

# [[Cookbook:boil|Boil]] the fresh spinach leaves and the salt in the water for about 5 minutes. If you use frozen spinach, follow the instructions on the box.
# Drain away the water, and let the spinach dry for a minute or so.
# Put the spinach back into the [[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|pan]] and add the cream. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] for a few more minutes.
# Add salt and pepper to taste.

=== Variation II – Chopped spinach ===

# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the fresh spinach leaves as in variation I, or gently thaw the frozen chopped spinach in a little bit of water in a pan. 
# Mix the flour with the chopped spinach in the pan, and add the milk. 
# Bring the spinach to the boil, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] gently for 3–5 minutes. 
# Add salt and pepper to taste.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* It is not uncommon to add a dash of [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]] and/or [[Cookbook:nutmeg|nutmeg]] to the creamed spinach.
* The proportions of milk/cream to spinach can be varied to produce anything from a rich green color to something similar to a [[Cookbook:White Sauce|white sauce]] with spinach in it, all according to taste.
* Note that spinach is high in nitrites, which means you may not have to use as much salt as you might think.
